Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 139 s. 2022 October 27, 2022 MR. PATRICK JAMES L. GO President ARN Central Development Corporation Suite 1712, iCommerce Center 1712 Medical Plaza Ortigas Building, 25 San Miguel Avenue, Ortigas Center, Pasig City Dear Mr. Go: This has reference to your letter dated October II, 2022 requesting for this Department's guidance and assistance on whether local government units must comply with the terms and conditions under duly executed contract, like the subject Joint Venture Agreement (JVA). In your letter, you stated that ARN Central development Corporation (ACDC) is a domestic corporation which submitted an unsolicited proposal to undertake the design, financing, construction, operation and maintenance of an integrated solid waste management and treatment facility (hereinafter referred to as the "Project") to the Municipality of Silang, Cavite (hereinafter referred to as the "Municipality'). The said Project was to be undertaken through a JVA pursuant to the Municipality of Silang, Cavite P4 Code, which provides for the public-private partnership policy of the Municipality. After undergoing the required Competitive or Swiss Challenge, the Sangguniang Bayan ("SB") of Silang resolved to enter into a JV with ACDC for the Project. Correspondingly, on 15 February 2022, the SB of Silang issued a Resolution authorizing the local chief executive to enter into a JV Agreement of the Project with the Corporation. The JVA was signed by ACDC through its President and the Municipality, through its former Mayor Socorro Rosario F. Poblete. Thereafter, ACDC commenced the necessary operations to facilitate the construction of the facility. However, during the May 2022 elections, a new local chief executive was elected for the Municipality. Subsequently, ACDC received several letters from the Office of the Mayor regarding supposed violations committed by ACDC in the implementation of the Project. Unfortunately, while ACDC exerted its best efforts in complying with the "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

directives of the Municipality, it still received a notice from the Office of the Mayor to rescind the JVA. In this regard, you highlighted to the Municipality the provisions regarding rescission which provides for a dispute resolution and arbitration clause, further asserting that the Municipality should be bound to comply with the said clause in good faith, and that the Mayor should have referred any supposed disputes involving the Project for dispute resolution and arbitration, instead of immediately rescinding the same. Likewise, ACDC claims that the Mayor has violated the terms and conditions of the JVA, to the prejudice of the corporation. Under this premise arose your request for this Department's guidance and assistance on whether or not local government units must comply with the terms and conditions under duly executed contract, like the subject JVA. At the outset, we deem it proper to highlight the definition of a Joint Venture, which is a contractual arrangement whereby a Private Sector Partner (PSP) or a group of PSPs on one hand, and the local government unit (LGU) on the other hand, contribute money/ capital, service, assets (including equipment, land, intellectual property or anything of value), or a combination of any or all of the foregoing. Accordingly, as we have previously opined, there is no specific statute on PPP nor guidelines on Joint Ventures for local governments, and that a duly enacted local legislation (PPP Code) must be complied with in undertaking its PPP projects. Further, in another legal opinion , we explained that the LGU's discretion is consistent with the state policy of local autonomy and is in line with the operative principle of decentralization and the national goal of propelling social and economic growth and development through the active participation of the private sector. In this regard, in a contractual joint venture, the governing laws are the provisions of the New Civil Code of the Philippines on partnerships and contracts, considering that it is akin to partnerships, as well as the local PPP or Joint Venture Ordinance. Correspondingly, under our civil laws, a contract is the law between the parties. Obligations arising from contracts have the force of law between the contracting parties and should be complied with in good faith. Unless the stipulations in a contract are contrary to law, morals, good customs, public order or public policy, the same are binding as between the parties. In other words, the agreement or contract between the parties is the formal expression of the parties' rights, duties and obligations. Thus, when the terms of an agreement have been reduced to writing, it is considered as containing all the terms agreed upon and there can be no evidence of such terms other than the contents of the written agreement between the parties and their successors in interest. In view thereof, we are of the view that the JVA between ACDC and the Municipality is governed by the provisions in their agreement, which includes the clause on dispute resolution and arbitration regarding any disagreement, dispute, controversy, Or claim arising out of, or in connection with, the breach, termination, invalidity, or interpretation of the agreement. Page 2 of 3

Hence, the change of administration cannot detract the parties to comply with the agreements set forth in the contract. The parties also cannot unilaterally rescind the contract, any action to do the same should be thru the appropriate courts. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY THE AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: AN R R. LLAMAS AT n rsecretary or External, Legal and Legislative Affairs SELLNJVRULLLS-LRALLD/rjki copy furnished: RD ARIEL O.
